requirements.subject: ent:configuration-operation
requirements.canonical: A configuration operation IS an operation used to set up and control test components and their connections.
requirements.original: Configuration operations are used to set up and control test components and their connections.

requirements.subject: ent:configuration-operation
requirements.canonical: A configuration operation SHALL only be used in a test case, or in behaviour invoked directly or indirectly from a test case or from behaviour started on a PTC.
requirements.original: a) These operations shall only be used in: TTCN-3 test cases; behaviour invoked directly or indirectly from a test case or from behaviour started on a PTC.

readings: Every operation of table 20 (including `mtc`, `system` and `self`) SHALL only be used in a test case or in behaviour invoked directly or indirectly from a test case or from behaviour started on a PTC.

Only the operations that set up or change the test configuration (connect, map, create, start, ...) SHALL be restricted to test cases and behaviour invoked from them; the reference operations are not covered.
ambiguity.issue: 'These operations' may refer to all operations of table 20 or only to the configuration-changing ones; chose the first reading because table 20 lists all of them as configuration operations.

requirements.subject: ent:configuration-operation
requirements.canonical: A configuration operation SHALL NOT be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: b) They shall not be present in: control behaviour; declarations inside component type definitions; or functions invoked directly or indirectly from declarations inside component type definitions.

ambiguity.issue: Item b) uses 'shall not be present in', item a) uses 'shall only be used in'; same meaning assumed.

requirements.subject: ent:configuration-operation
requirements.canonical: A configuration operation SHALL NOT be used in a declaration inside a component type definition.
requirements.original: b) They shall not be present in: control behaviour; declarations inside component type definitions; or functions invoked directly or indirectly from declarations inside component type definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:configuration-operation
requirements.canonical: A configuration operation SHALL NOT be used in a function invoked directly or indirectly from a declaration inside a component type definition.
requirements.original: b) They shall not be present in: control behaviour; declarations inside component type definitions; or functions invoked directly or indirectly from declarations inside component type definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:connect-operation
requirements.canonical: The `connect` operation IS connecting a port of one test component to a port of another test component.
requirements.original: Operation: Connect; Explanation: Connects the port of one test component to the port of another test component; Syntax Examples: connect(ptc1:p1, ptc2:p2);

requirements.subject: ent:connect-operation
requirements.canonical: The `connect` operation has the syntax `connect(ComponentRef:Port, ComponentRef:Port)`, e.g. `connect(ptc1:p1, ptc2:p2);`.
requirements.original: Operation: Connect; Explanation: Connects the port of one test component to the port of another test component; Syntax Examples: connect(ptc1:p1, ptc2:p2);

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: The `disconnect` operation IS disconnecting two or more connected ports.
requirements.original: Operation: Disconnect; Explanation: Disconnects two or more connected ports; Syntax Examples: disconnect(ptc1:p1, ptc2:p2);

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: The `disconnect` operation has the syntax `disconnect(ComponentRef:Port, ComponentRef:Port)`, e.g. `disconnect(ptc1:p1, ptc2:p2);`.
requirements.original: Operation: Disconnect; Explanation: Disconnects two or more connected ports; Syntax Examples: disconnect(ptc1:p1, ptc2:p2);

requirements.subject: ent:map-operation
requirements.canonical: The `map` operation IS mapping a port of one test component to a port of the test system interface.
requirements.original: Operation: Map; Explanation: Maps the port of one test component to the port of the test system interface; Syntax Examples: map(ptc1:q, system:sutPort1);

requirements.subject: ent:map-operation
requirements.canonical: The `map` operation has the syntax `map(ComponentRef:Port, system:Port)`, e.g. `map(ptc1:q, system:sutPort1);`.
requirements.original: Operation: Map; Explanation: Maps the port of one test component to the port of the test system interface; Syntax Examples: map(ptc1:q, system:sutPort1);

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-operation
requirements.canonical: The `unmap` operation IS unmapping two or more mapped ports.
requirements.original: Operation: Unmap; Explanation: Unmaps two or more mapped ports; Syntax Examples: unmap(ptc1:q, system:sutPort1);

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-operation
requirements.canonical: The `unmap` operation has the syntax `unmap(ComponentRef:Port, system:Port)`, e.g. `unmap(ptc1:q, system:sutPort1);`.
requirements.original: Operation: Unmap; Explanation: Unmaps two or more mapped ports; Syntax Examples: unmap(ptc1:q, system:sutPort1);

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The `create` operation IS creating a normal (non-alive) or an alive test component.
requirements.original: **Operation** **Explanation** **Syntax Examples** **Test Component Operations** Create Creation of a normal or alive test Non-alive test components: component, the distinction between `var PTCType c := PTCType.create;` normal and alive test components is Alive test components: made during creation `var PTCType c := PTCType.create` `alive;` (MTC behaves as a normal test component)

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The distinction between a normal and an alive test component IS made when the test component is created.
requirements.original: **Operation** **Explanation** **Syntax Examples** **Test Component Operations** Create Creation of a normal or alive test Non-alive test components: component, the distinction between `var PTCType c := PTCType.create;` normal and alive test components is Alive test components: made during creation `var PTCType c := PTCType.create` `alive;` (MTC behaves as a normal test component)

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The MTC IS behaving as a normal (non-alive) test component.
requirements.original: **Operation** **Explanation** **Syntax Examples** **Test Component Operations** Create Creation of a normal or alive test Non-alive test components: component, the distinction between `var PTCType c := PTCType.create;` normal and alive test components is Alive test components: made during creation `var PTCType c := PTCType.create` `alive;` (MTC behaves as a normal test component)

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The `create` operation has the syntax `ComponentType.create` for non-alive and `ComponentType.create alive` for alive test components, e.g. `var PTCType c := PTCType.create alive;`.
requirements.original: **Operation** **Explanation** **Syntax Examples** **Test Component Operations** Create Creation of a normal or alive test Non-alive test components: component, the distinction between `var PTCType c := PTCType.create;` normal and alive test components is Alive test components: made during creation `var PTCType c := PTCType.create` `alive;` (MTC behaves as a normal test component)

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `start` test component operation IS starting test behaviour on a test component.
requirements.original: Start Starting test behaviour on a test `c.start(PTCBehaviour());` component, starting behaviour does not affect the status of component variables, timers or ports

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Starting behaviour on a test component IS NOT affecting the status of the component variables, component timers or component ports of that test component.
requirements.original: Start Starting test behaviour on a test `c.start(PTCBehaviour());` component, starting behaviour does not affect the status of component variables, timers or ports

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `start` test component operation has the syntax `ComponentRef.start(FunctionInstance)`, e.g. `c.start(PTCBehaviour());`.
requirements.original: Start Starting test behaviour on a test `c.start(PTCBehaviour());` component, starting behaviour does not affect the status of component variables, timers or ports

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `stop` test component operation IS stopping the test behaviour running on a test component.
requirements.original: Stop Stopping test behaviour on a test `c.stop;` component

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `stop` test component operation has the syntax `ComponentRef.stop`, e.g. `c.stop;`.
requirements.original: Stop Stopping test behaviour on a test `c.stop;` component

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` test component operation IS causing a test component to cease to exist.
requirements.original: Kill Causes a test component to cease to `c.kill;` exist

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` test component operation has the syntax `ComponentRef.kill`, e.g. `c.kill;`.
requirements.original: Kill Causes a test component to cease to `c.kill;` exist

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `alive` operation IS returning `true` if the test component has been created and is ready to execute or is already executing behaviour.
requirements.original: Alive Returns true if the test component has `if (c.alive) …` been created and is ready to execute or is already executingbehaviour; otherwise returns false

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `alive` operation IS returning `false` if the test component has not been created, or is neither ready to execute nor executing behaviour.
requirements.original: Alive Returns true if the test component has `if (c.alive) …` been created and is ready to execute or is already executingbehaviour; otherwise returns false

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `alive` operation has the syntax `ComponentRef.alive` and is a Boolean expression, e.g. `if (c.alive) …`.
requirements.original: Alive Returns true if the test component has `if (c.alive) …` been created and is ready to execute or is already executingbehaviour; otherwise returns false

requirements.subject: ent:running-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `running` test component operation IS returning `true` as long as the test component is executing behaviour.
requirements.original: Running Returns true as long as the test `if (c.running) …` component is executing behaviour; otherwise returns false

requirements.subject: ent:running-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `running` test component operation IS returning `false` when the test component is not executing behaviour.
requirements.original: Running Returns true as long as the test `if (c.running) …` component is executing behaviour; otherwise returns false

requirements.subject: ent:running-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `running` test component operation has the syntax `ComponentRef.running` and is a Boolean expression, e.g. `if (c.running) …`.
requirements.original: Running Returns true as long as the test `if (c.running) …` component is executing behaviour; otherwise returns false

requirements.subject: ent:done-operation
requirements.canonical: The `done` operation IS checking whether the function running on a test component has terminated.
requirements.original: Done Checks whether the function running on a test component has terminated

requirements.subject: ent:done-operation
requirements.canonical: The `done` operation has the syntax `ComponentRef.done`, e.g. `c.done;`.
requirements.original: Done Checks whether the function running on a test component has terminated

requirements.subject: ent:killed-operation
requirements.canonical: The `killed` operation IS checking whether a test component has ceased to exist.
requirements.original: Killed Checks whether a component has `c.killed { … }` ceased to exist

ambiguity.issue: 'component' is used where 'test component' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:killed-operation
requirements.canonical: The `killed` operation has the syntax `ComponentRef.killed`, e.g. `c.killed { … }` as an alternative.
requirements.original: Killed Checks whether a component has `c.killed { … }` ceased to exist

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The `testcase.stop` operation IS terminating the test case with the test verdict `error`.
requirements.original: **Test Case Operations** Stop Terminates the test case with the test `testcase.stop ( … );` verdict error

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The `testcase.stop` operation has the syntax `testcase.stop(…)` with an optional log argument list, e.g. `testcase.stop ( … );`.
requirements.original: **Test Case Operations** Stop Terminates the test case with the test `testcase.stop ( … );` verdict error

requirements.subject: ent:mtc-operation
requirements.canonical: The `mtc` operation IS returning the reference to the MTC.
requirements.original: **Reference Operations** Mtc Gets the reference to the MTC `connect(mtc:p, ptc:p);` System Gets the reference to the test system `map(c:p, system:sutPort);` interface

requirements.subject: ent:mtc-operation
requirements.canonical: The `mtc` operation has the syntax `mtc`, usable as a component reference, e.g. `connect(mtc:p, ptc:p);`.
requirements.original: **Reference Operations** Mtc Gets the reference to the MTC `connect(mtc:p, ptc:p);` System Gets the reference to the test system `map(c:p, system:sutPort);` interface

requirements.subject: ent:system-operation
requirements.canonical: The `system` operation IS returning the reference to the test system interface.
requirements.original: **Reference Operations** Mtc Gets the reference to the MTC `connect(mtc:p, ptc:p);` System Gets the reference to the test system `map(c:p, system:sutPort);` interface

requirements.subject: ent:system-operation
requirements.canonical: The `system` operation has the syntax `system`, usable as a component reference, e.g. `map(c:p, system:sutPort);`.
requirements.original: **Reference Operations** Mtc Gets the reference to the MTC `connect(mtc:p, ptc:p);` System Gets the reference to the test system `map(c:p, system:sutPort);` interface

requirements.subject: ent:self-operation
requirements.canonical: The `self` operation IS returning the reference to the test component that executes the `self` operation.
requirements.original: Self Gets the reference to the test component that executes this operation

requirements.subject: ent:self-operation
requirements.canonical: The `self` operation has the syntax `self`, usable as a component reference, e.g. `self.stop;`.
requirements.original: Self Gets the reference to the test component that executes this operation
